records.title: Nonequilibrium Molecular Dynamics Study of Interfacial Thermal Transport at Micro/Nanoscales
records.summary: The 4th Graduate Academic Forum of the Chinese Society of Micro-Nano Technology, Keynote talk, Forum Chair

fields.Event: The 4th Graduate Academic Forum of the Chinese Society of Micro-Nano Technology

records.search_text: Thermal transport at micro- and nanoscales is jointly governed by interfacial interactions, spatial confinement effects, and characteristic length scales, and conventional continuum heat conduction models based on Fourier's law may no longer be applicable to such systems. Using nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, this talk systematically investigates thermal transport across vacuum nanogaps and solid–liquid interfaces. At subnanometer separations, quasi-Casimir coupling can induce phonon transmission between two solid surfaces, while interfacial thermal resonance provides efficient pathways for energy transfer. For SiC nanogaps, analyses of vibrational spectra and local heat flux reveal that identical atomic surface terminations can enhance heat transfer by improving interfacial phonon matching. In addition, a negative electric field can modulate the vibrational displacements of interfacial atoms and strengthen tunneling channels dominated by optical phonons. For solid–liquid interfacial systems, this study further examines the scale dependence of Kapitza length from the nanoscale to the microscale under constant heat flux and constant temperature difference conditions, identifying three distinct regimes of solid–liquid interfacial thermal transport: the phonon-dominated, transition, and conduction regimes. These findings provide a unified multiscale framework for understanding interfacial thermal transport and a theoretical basis for designing thermal management systems at micro- and nanoscales.

records.title: Study on Mechanism of Quasi-Casimir Coupling Driven Extreme Near-Field Heat Transfer in Two-Dimensional Indium Selenide
records.summary: National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), Young Scientists Fund (Category C) (PI) 2027.01–2029.12
records.search_text:
Extreme near-field heat transfer is a key fundamental issue in the thermal management of two-dimensional semiconductor devices and is of considerable importance for understanding nonconventional thermal transport in low-dimensional systems. Within nanogaps, in addition to near-field radiation, quasi-Casimir coupling arising from intermolecular interactions can induce heat transfer across the nanogaps and interfacial thermal resonance in bulk materials. However, the underlying mechanisms governing gap-dependent thermal transport in two-dimensional van der Waals materials has not yet been systematically clarified.

This project focuses on indium selenide (InSe) nanofilms, a representative two-dimensional polar material featuring high carrier mobility and strong polarization characteristics. Using first-principles data-driven machine-learning potentials in combination with nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, the project aims to elucidate the mechanisms of extreme near-field heat transfer in InSe nanofilms.

By constructing controllable nanogap models and employing local heat flux decomposition, the respective contributions of long-range and short-range interactions to heat flux will be quantitatively resolved and regime classification criterion will be established. By further tuning atomic termination configurations, the project will reveal how variations in interfacial coupling strength regulate thermal transport channels, thereby developing structure-based design principles for passive thermal management.

In addition, external electric fields will be introduced to clarify the nonlinear dependence of interfacial thermal conductance on the strength and direction of electric field, enabling active thermal management.

This project will establish a mechanistic framework for quasi-Casimir coupling driven heat transfer across nanogaps in two-dimensional van der Waals materials, thereby providing a solid theoretical foundation for the industrial application of thermal management in high power density chips.
Fund: National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), Young Scientists Fund (Category C)

Upholding the vision of a community with a shared future for mankind, the Program advocates and practices the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, and the Global Civilization Initiative, and promotes the building of an Innovation Silk Road under the Belt and Road Initiative. Following the principles of selecting the best candidates, people-centeredness, openness and inclusiveness, and equality with mutual learning, the Program provides funding support for eligible outstanding young international scientists, scholars, and researchers (hereinafter referred to as “Talented Young Scientist”) to come to China for work and exchange. The Program aims to enhance the scientific research capacity and innovation capacity of partner countries, promote science/technology and humanities exchanges between China and countries around the world, provide a high-quality platform for young scientists to learn from each other, build long-term and stable S&T cooperative partnerships with relevant countries, and pool consensus and strength to foster people-to-people connectivity.

records.title: Exploration of quasi-Casimir coupling induced phonon heat transfer mechanism by deep learning
records.summary: Kyushu Institute of Technology Project for Discovery of Advanced Themes (PI) 2024.04–2025.03
records.search_text:
As part of the global climate change response, advanced thermal management techniques at the nanoscale are required to achieve high energy conversion efficiencies. The applicant has discovered a thermal resonance phenomenon through quasi-Casimir coupling, in which two solids sandwiched in a vacuum nanogap of several molecular layers realize phonon transport only through intermolecular interactions. This new phonon heat transfer mechanism is characterized by the fact that it does not require an electromagnetic field, since the phonon transport is induced by quasi-Casimir coupling between two solid surfaces. In other words, only phonons are allowed to transmit and not electrons, which makes the heat transfer efficiency higher than that of near-field thermal radiation or Casimir heat transfer. The aim of this study is to clarify the principles of innovative nanoscale thermal management techniques for ultra-small localized regions based on the phonon heat transfer mechanism induced by quasi-Casimir coupling in the nanogap through molecular dynamics simulations and deep learning.
Fund: Kyushu Institute of Technology Project for Discovery of Advanced Themes

The enthusiasm and passion exhibited by the students are truly commendable, and I look forward to the prospect of continued exchange programs between our faculties and students. To the talented UM students, I extend a warm invitation to consider the opportunities for study at Kyutech.
I express my heartfelt gratitude for the efforts put forth by the UMPADEC team in facilitating these experiences. Your warm welcome and support have made my visit exceptionally memorable. I am confident that these interactions have laid the foundation for strong bonds between our institutions.
We eagerly anticipate further interactions and collaborations that will undoubtedly strengthen the ties between the Kyushu Institute of Technology and the University of Malaya. Together, we can propel academic excellence and innovation to new heights.

records.summary: Online Sakura Science 2022
records.search_text:
An online event has been held by Heat Transfer Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering at Kyushu Institute of Technology under SAKURA Exchange Program in Science by Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST) from Nov. 14th to Dec. 26.
More than 100 participants who were invited to this online exchange program are from Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, National Taiwan University of Science and Technology, Nanyang Technological University Singapore, University of Ulsan, Qingdao University of Technology, Northeastern University (CN), Shandong University, and Qilu University of Technology. They positively gave presentations at International Joint Seminar on Mechanical Engineering 2022, joined online laboratory tours, and finished collaborative works by making spins and windmills with Japanese students.
This online event enhanced the international exchange among all the participants. Kyutech will keep the relationship with its partner universities for education development.
Link: https://www.kyutech.ac.jp/whats-new/topics/entry-9643.html

records.title: Thermal resonance induced by quasi-Casimir coupling for innovative nanoscale thermal management
records.summary: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), Grant-in-Aid for Research Activity Start-up (PI) 2022.08–2024.03
records.search_text:
Phonon heat transfer can be induced by quasi-Casimir coupling due to molecular interaction across a nanogap without electromagnetic fields. However, the quasi-Casimir coupling between the nanostructures and adsorbed water layers on the solid surfaces is still open for question. Therefore, we will verify phonon transmission across a nanogap via nanostructures and adsorbed water layers, focusing on quasi-Casimir coupling and thermal resonance.
Fund: Grant-in-Aid for Research Activity Start-up

records.title: Innovative nanoscale thermal management by quasi-Casimir coupling induced phonon transport
records.summary: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), Grant-in-Aid for Challenging Research (Exploratory) (Core Participant) 2022.06–2025.03
records.search_text:
Thermal resonance phenomenon by quasi-Casimir coupling has been discovered, in which phonon transport is realized by only intermolecular interactions between two solids sandwiched by a vacuum nanogap of a few molecular layers. Based on the quasi-Casimir coupling induced phonon heat transfer in the nanogap, this study aims to clarify the principle of innovative nanoscale thermal management technology in the ultra-small local region by both molecular dynamics simulations and experiments.
Fund: Grant-in-Aid for Challenging Research (Exploratory)

records.title: Solid-liquid-vapor interfacial transport phenomena coupled with wetting/condensation/evaporation
records.summary: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (B) (Core Participant) 2022.04–2025.03
records.search_text:
Highly efficient energy conversion and utilization technologies are closely related to phase change phenomena such as macroscopic condensation, evaporation, and boiling through the solid-liquid-vapour interface. On the other hand, the effect of interfacial resistance due to the properties of the heat transfer surface relatively increases as the representative dimensions of the target system become smaller with the development of nano- and micro-technologies. In this study, we develop a microscopic heat and mass transfer model that takes into account the interfacial resistance at the solid-liquid-vapour interface.
Fund: Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (B)

records.title: Solid-liquid-vapor interfacial resistance related multiphysis of tribology
records.summary: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (B) (Participant) 2018.04–2021.03
records.search_text:
Scale effect of the interfacial resistance at solid－liquid－vapor interface increases as increasing the characteristic length scale of the system, which might induce a significant deviation in microsystems from the classical heat transfer theory for macrosystem. In this study, the correlation between the interfacial resistance and the thermal/wetting/electrochemical properties at solid－liquid－vapor interface has been studied. The effects of interfacial resistances on thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication were investigated to clarify the temperature rise and film thickness reduction of tribological surfaces under point contact.
Fund: Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (B)
